title: Benefic and malefic planets: why the question needs your lagna | Ask Tota
description: Natural benefic and functional benefic are two different systems, and they routinely disagree. Here is how both work, plus kendradhipati dosha and the upachaya exception.
og_title: Is Saturn bad? The question needs your lagna first
og_description: Natural and functional classifications are separate systems that disagree constantly. Here is how each works, and why a malefic can be your best graha.
h1: “is saturn bad” is not a question u can answer
dek: not without a lagna. natural benefic and functional benefic are two separate systems, they disagree constantly, and one of them says a harsh graha can be the best thing in ur chart. here is how both work.

faq.a: jupiter and venus always, the waxing moon, and mercury when it keeps good company. the classical word is shubha, meaning gentle or auspicious in effect.
saturn, mars, the sun, rahu and ketu, plus the waning moon and mercury when it sits with malefics. the word is krura or papa, meaning harsh, not evil.

faq.q: why do the moon and mercury change sides?
faq.a: they are the two conditional grahas. the moon is benefic when waxing and malefic when waning, measured by its distance from the sun. mercury takes the character of whatever it sits with.

a graha that rules good houses for ur particular ascendant. the trikona lords, of the 1st, 5th and 9th, are the reliable ones. this classification depends entirely on ur lagna and it routinely contradicts the natural one.

a natural benefic that rules a kendra, meaning the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th house, loses its benefic power. a natural malefic ruling a kendra gains strength instead. it is one of the more counterintuitive rules in the system.

a single graha that rules both a kendra and a trikona for ur lagna, making it the most helpful graha in that chart. six lagnas have one: saturn for vrishabha and tula, mars for karka and simha, venus for makara and kumbha.
the 6th, 8th and 12th, called dusthanas. their lords are generally treated as functionally difficult, though a graha ruling both a dusthana and a good house is a mixed case rather than a bad one.
the 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th. malefics are said to improve in them over time, which is why mars in the 6th and saturn in the 11th read well despite both grahas being classed as harsh.
the lords of the 2nd and 7th houses are called marakas, associated with the end of things in the longevity tradition. it is a technical classification and it is regularly misused to frighten people.

faq.q: so is saturn good or bad?
faq.a: for a vrishabha or tula ascendant it is the yogakaraka, the single most helpful graha in the chart. for others it rules difficult houses. the question has no answer until someone knows ur lagna.

faq.q: does a benefic in a bad house become bad?
faq.a: it complicates rather than reverses. a natural benefic in the 6th or 8th is usually read as a softening influence in a difficult area, while a graha ruling those houses carries their significations wherever it goes.

most practitioners weight the functional one more heavily, because it is specific to ur chart. the natural classification describes temperament, and the functional one describes what a graha is actually delivering for u.
